title: TrailGenic Seven Day Aftereffect Dataset
description: Day-2 restoration is common but not universal. Historical recovery inflection is preserved; Elbert closed successfully, Pikes failed recovery closure, and Wheeler showed partial recovery after compressed stacking.

records.mechanism: Western Altitude Block update through Wheeler Peak
physiological_response: Day-2 restoration is common but not universal. Historical recovery inflection is preserved; Elbert closed successfully, Pikes failed recovery closure, and Wheeler showed partial recovery after compressed stacking.
adaptation_outcomes: The adaptation remained; the compressed block exceeded the current recovery envelope.

records.mechanism: Day-2 autonomic supercompensation following high-load fasted alpine effort

stimulus.inflection_session: Session 16 — Baldy via Devil's Backbone, March 29, 2026
stimulus.session_context: high-load fasted alpine effort with post-effort Day-1 and Day-2 biomarker capture

physiological_response: Day-2 HRV returns at or above pre-hike baseline.
Day-2 resting HR matches or beats pre-hike baseline.
Sleep architecture restored within the 48-hour post-effort window.
adaptation_outcomes: Seven consecutive Day-2 AUTONOMIC_RESTORED reads across five trail systems.
Transition from recovery cost to recovery compounding.
Session 16 marks the first durable recovery inflection in the 22-session dataset.

supporting_science.finding: Post-exercise molecular signaling can persist beyond the exercise bout and contribute to training adaptation.
HRV recovery dynamics can serve as a marker of endurance adaptation and autonomic readiness.

records.mechanism: Pre-hike sleep state gates Day-1 recovery architecture independently of Day-2 supercompensation

stimulus.pre_hike_sleep_state: compromised pre-hike sleep with compressed duration and REM

physiological_response: Day-1 returns to AUTONOMIC_STRAINED with elevated resting HR and suppressed HRV.
Day-2 fully restores after the acute sleep-gated Day-1 recovery cost.
The same trained system can show Day-1 strain and Day-2 supercompensation in sequence.
adaptation_outcomes: Day-2 recovery is durable and route-independent.
Day-1 architecture is conditional on entering rested.
Pre-hike sleep becomes a gating variable rather than a secondary lifestyle covariate.

supporting_science.finding: Sleep quantity and quality materially influence athletic recovery and subsequent performance readiness.
Autonomic recovery markers help identify whether training load has been absorbed.

records.mechanism: Suprabaseline rebound from worst pre-hike state to highest exit state within 48 hours

stimulus.session: San Gorgonio via Vivian Creek, May 9, 2026

physiological_response: Resting HR at 54 bpm matching all-time Day-2 low.
Recovery arc moved from suppressed pre-hike autonomic state to highest exit state within 48 hours.
adaptation_outcomes: Largest positive recovery arc in 22-session dataset.
System actively converts effort into adaptation faster than effort accumulates.
Apex session simultaneously set distance, altitude, duration, and recovery-arc ceilings.

supporting_science.finding: Repeated endurance stimuli can drive persistent signaling that supports adaptation after the effort ends.
Positive HRV rebound after load can indicate adaptive recovery rather than accumulated strain.

western_altitude_block_summary.interpretation: Normal cadence usually restored; compressed summit stacking exposed the current recovery boundary.
